# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 6 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 6
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. When therefore he gave the commandment, what did he say? "Who is he who strives with me? Let him stand against me. Or who is he who strives with me in judgment? Let him draw near to the Lord's child."
2. "Woe to you, for all of you will grow old as a garment, and the moth will consume you."
3. And again the prophet says, since he was set as a strong stone for crushing: "Behold, I am laying as a foundation in Zion a precious cornerstone, chosen, honored; and the one who hopes in him shall live forever."
4. Then what? Is our hope built upon a stone? Far from it. But the Lord has set his flesh in strength. For he says: "And he set me as a hard rock."
5. And the prophet says again: "The stone which the builders rejected — this has become the head of the corner." And again: "This is the great and wonderful day which the Lord made."
6. I write to you more simply so that you may understand; I am a poor slave of your love.
7. See then what he says: "And he set me as a hard rock." This rock and this stone — what is it? The prophet says: "And there was set a stone in Zion, and it shall be destroyed, and the glory of it is of the living."
8. Since then the flesh of the Lord will have to suffer, it was necessary that when there was no tree of life but only a tree of death that what was then corruptible should be revealed as life.
9. For since we have sinned, all things are dying. What the Lord endured did not, however, cease from working.
10. For since Adam transgressed with a wrong intention, death reigned. And what was written in Genesis was: "You shall eat from every tree in the garden," and then: "But from the tree from which the knowledge of good and evil is, you shall not eat" — and from it we have learned.
11. Do you understand what Barnabas is saying? But he also introduces another kind of knowledge with great wisdom. See, he says: We who eat from the tree of life, from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil — this is what it means: those of us who believe and who hear in hope of his cross, we shall not die. But those who disobey will die.
12. The reason the law says: "You shall not eat from it" is that he who at the beginning planted the tree of knowledge, himself is now the tree of life.
